taste.name: Headline as state indicator
taste.trigger: When presenting 4-6 parallel product features in one section
taste.decision: Chose a stacked list of full-size display headlines where only the active one turns ink (#0B051D) and the rest sit at #C4C3CA/#96959F, over tabs, icon grids or carousels with arrows
taste.reason: Because a reader sees the entire menu of options at once and the scroll position itself tells them where they are; no control needs to be learned
evidence: 52-100px Klarna Title headlines rendered in #96959F/#C4C3CA when inactive
active item gains a 16px body paragraph + 9999px pill CTA
same device used twice: 'Designed around you…' sticky list and 'Payments / Cards / Memberships…' centered list

taste.name: Depth from radius and photography, not shadow
taste.trigger: When separating media blocks from a white page
taste.decision: Chose 32-48px corner radius on photo cards and zero borders/shadows, over elevated cards with drop shadows or outlined containers
taste.reason: Because large soft corners read as physical objects (a phone, a card) while keeping the page flat and fast to scan
evidence: only 1 shadow value on 6 elements (0 2px 4px rgba(0,0,0,.1))
white #FFFFFF covers 88.5% of surface; no section dividers, sections separated by 80px gaps

taste.name: Pink is a signal, ink does the work
taste.trigger: When choosing how much brand color to spread across the page
taste.decision: Chose to keep pink #FFA8CD to ~0.3% of surface (one hero CTA, the app widget, the selected option) and put every other CTA in ink #0B051D, over a pink-washed page or pink headings
taste.reason: Because a scarce color is instantly read as 'this is the thing to press'; the brand stays recognisable without tiring the eye
evidence: mint #C1F4D1 restricted to cashback data badges

taste.name: Extreme scale contrast between two widths
taste.decision: Chose a condensed heavy display face at 64-100px with ~0.95 line-height against a 16-20px regular text face, over a single family with moderate 1.25x steps
taste.reason: Because condensed letters let short, confident sentences fill the width at poster size, so a page with little copy still feels loud and specific
evidence: footer wordmark spans the full 1380px width
